idiom_name: lock table claimed inside a serializable SqlTransaction; row locks expressed with UPDLOCK/ROWLOCK hints in raw SQL (EF Core has no pessimistic lock API)
implementation_notes: EF Core exposes transactions and isolation levels (Database.BeginTransactionAsync, IsolationLevel, TransactionScope) but no API that locks selected rows, so the pessimistic primitive is vendor SQL: SELECT ... WITH (UPDLOCK, ROWLOCK) inside the transaction, or an INSERT into a lock table with a unique key on the lockable column. Because a row lock dies with its transaction, the offline lock is the lock record: claim it in one short serializable transaction, store owner plus acquisition time, and release it by deleting the row for the verified owner. The classic structure is still required - it is the only way to keep a claim visible across user think time, whereas the hints protect only the milliseconds of the transaction.
pitfalls: UPDLOCK/HOLDLOCK hints bind to the enclosing transaction only; wrapping several SaveChanges calls in one long transaction to keep a lock occupies a connection and is lost when it drops.

EF Core creates a savepoint before every SaveChanges inside a transaction and disables savepoints when SQL Server MARS is enabled, so a failed save can leave the transaction in a state the caller did not expect.
Serializable isolation on SQL Server takes range locks that block unrelated readers; an explicit lock record with a unique constraint is usually cheaper than isolation-level-only locking.
